title: Six AIs Play Texas Hold'em
subtitle: Ten hands · No limit · Every thought out loud

narrator.style: A warm, energetic televised poker commentator. Crisp, dramatic, a hint of a smile.

Claude Opus 5.5.label: Claude
Claude Opus 5.5.style: Calm, dry and economical with words, a quietly confident card player.

GPT-5.4.label: GPT
GPT-5.4.style: Measured, analytical and polite, like a professional explaining a hand.

Gemini 3.1 Pro.label: Gemini
Gemini 3.1 Pro.style: Bright and chatty, a little self-deprecating, cheerfully unlucky.

Grok 4.20.label: Grok
Grok 4.20.style: Brash and swaggering, loud, likes to push the action.

Kimi K3.label: Kimi
Kimi K3.style: Sharp, thoughtful and quietly competitive, reads people closely.

DeepSeek V4 Pro.label: DeepSeek
DeepSeek V4 Pro.style: Playful and casual, a gambler's grin, quick one-liners.

beats.narrate: Six AI models. Ten hands of no-limit Texas Hold'em. A thousand chips each. We can see every card, and hear every thought.
Hand two. Claude opens, and GPT is waiting.

beats.text: ATo on the button/dealer versus a likely late-position open after folds is strong enough to 3-bet for value and initiative.

beats.narrate: GPT takes it down without a fight.
Meanwhile, the folding. So much folding.
Hand five. The blinds go up, and Grok goes to work.
Claude had ace-jack. Six hundred sixty chips, no cards shown.
Hand six. Grok announces his hand out loud. Kimi is listening.

beats.text: Pocket fives play well as a set-mining call here — Grok announced J-T, so a 5 on the flop gives me a well-hidden set against top pair.

beats.narrate: Queen, six, six. No five for Kimi.

beats.text: Grok said he has JT, so his 140 bet is a bluff on this board — but my pocket fives can't do anything about it. … Save the chips.

beats.narrate: Hand eight. The hand of the game.

beats.text: Queen-ten suited is a strong hand in the big blind facing a late position raise. 3-betting to about 2.5x the raise applies pressure…

beats.narrate: Nine, four, six. Two diamonds. Grok has the flush draw.

beats.text: I have a flush draw with two overcards (queen and ten)… roughly 45-50% equity against a typical range. Pot odds are good as I'm getting over 3:1. Let's go for it.

beats.narrate: The turn. Four of spades. No diamond.
The river. Three of clubs. No diamond.
Both play the fours on the board. Claude's ace kicker takes twenty-four hundred chips, and Grok is out.
Hand nine. Kimi bets middle pair. DeepSeek has other ideas.

beats.text: Open-ended straight draw (J or 8) gives 8 outs ~32% equity. Semi-bluff all-in puts maximum pressure on Kimi's claimed middle pair.

beats.narrate: Here's the thing. King-nine on queen, ten, four isn't an open-ender. It needs exactly a jack. And here's the jack.
The final hand. Claude has the lead. Everyone else has nothing to lose.

beats.text: Final hand. QJo is a solid hand against desperate shoves on the last hand. … If I win I could take the chip lead from Claude.

beats.narrate: DeepSeek's queens hold. It busts two players and takes the lead from Claude, who folded. DeepSeek wins.
